concerns: The headline quality claim rests on uncalibrated AI reviewers reading only the papers, with no human expert evaluation or calibration against human decisions, so workshop-level quality is not established.
The five-run sample with a single research model and no ablations cannot attribute outcomes to the question procedure, critic, or reviewer, leaving the central contribution underdetermined.

The post-hoc amendment counting the pilot after three results had been seen, and the post-hoc choice of PDF reviews as the main result after seeing Markdown reviews, introduce selection and reporting deviations that weaken the pre-registered evaluation.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the experimental logging, reproducibility framework, and candor regarding protocol deviations are commendable, the paper's substantive evaluation of scientific quality rests entirely on uncalibrated external LLM reviewers without human expert corroboration across only five runs. Under conservative curation standards, the lack of independent ground truth or human calibration for paper quality warrants an uncertain verdict.

research, but in those demonstrations humans chose the research area and selected the outputs
to show. We study letting the AI formulate the research question itself, and we report every
run. Our system gives an off-the-shelf coding agent an instruction document and two skills: one
for formulating the question, in which the agent diverges from recent technologies into problems
of other fields, screens its candidates for known failure modes and obtains a critique from a
different model; and one for peer review, in which a reviewer from another model family re-
runs the study from its records before the agent revises the paper. Over 13 development runs,
changes to the one or two sentences that set the research area coincided with large shifts in what

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The headline quality claim rests on uncalibrated AI reviewers reading only the papers, with no human expert evaluation or calibration against human decisions, so workshop-level quality is not established.
The five-run sample with a single research model and no ablations cannot attribute outcomes to the question procedure, critic, or reviewer, leaving the central contribution underdetermined.

The post-hoc amendment counting the pilot after three results had been seen, and the post-hoc choice of PDF reviews as the main result after seeing Markdown reviews, introduce selection and reporting deviations that weaken the pre-registered evaluation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The external reviewers come from model families other than the research agent and were not involved in drafting or revision, and the in-loop reviewer re-ran the studies from records to verify reproducibility.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External AI reviews by Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder, which read only the final papers and scored them on six axes with workshop and main-track judgments.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The in-loop critic (GPT-6-astra) and in-loop reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5) shaped the papers through critique adoption and revision, and the system was developed over 13 runs with instruction changes informed by post-run assessments.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of full autonomy from formulation to write-up and strict re-computability are supported by run records and deterministic replay scripts. However, claims regarding scientific quality and impact remain weakly corroborated due to reliance on uncalibrated LLM judges.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The primary evaluation relies on in-loop AI reviewer re-execution and external AI reviews by two separate LLMs (Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder), which rate papers at workshop level but low in novelty and clarity. However, sample size is limited to five runs, no human expert evaluation or comparison against human baselines is provided, and the pre-registration protocol underwent a post-hoc amendment to include the pilot run.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Re-execution and reproducibility checks were verified independently through executable scripts from clean git tags, and external review signals came from distinct model families not involved in drafting.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External automated reviews across 6 rubric axes and overall acceptance ratings from Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Internal multi-agent critique (GPT-6-astra) and in-loop execution review scoring (Claude Opus 5.5) that guide paper revision.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly disclose protocol deviations (post-hoc counting of the pilot run), sample size limits (five runs, single research model family), lack of human evaluation, and the tendency of agents to converge on narrow open-data resources.
primary.method_assessment: The pipeline links an orchestrator agent, a research agent (GPT-6.1-sol), a cross-model critic (GPT-6-astra), and an in-loop reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5) that re-runs code from deterministic records. The operational workflow, tool interactions, prompt skills, and record manifests are described in detail.
primary.quality_rationale: While the experimental logging, reproducibility framework, and candor regarding protocol deviations are commendable, the paper's substantive evaluation of scientific quality rests entirely on uncalibrated external LLM reviewers without human expert corroboration across only five runs. Under conservative curation standards, the lack of independent ground truth or human calibration for paper quality warrants an uncertain verdict.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents an autonomous AI research system where agents formulate their own research questions within a broadly specified domain (societal problems using open data), critique and review them via multi-agent interactions, and write fully reproducible reports across five consecutive runs.

During the claim extraction stage, CLAIMNOV
takes the title and description from the research
proposal P and produces, with an LLM (gpt-4o-
mini set to temperature 0), a list of contribution
claimsC P ={c 1, . . . , cm}.
Each claim ci is typed with a dimension dc and
an attribute-value pair (ca, cv). Dimensions are
drawn from {Problem, Methodology, Resource,
Result}, while an attribute represents the axis along
which two works can be compared. For instance,
for a Result claim, the attribute may be classifica-
tion accuracy on CIFAR-10, and the value may be
an improvement from 30.1% to 76.9%. We aim to
extract a small number of claims per proposal (2.4–
2.7 on average, the prompt allowing 1–4), based
on conventions in AI research. We process each
paper in the reference pool Π through this stage
once, using its abstract as the description text, to
produce pool claimsC Π.

During the claim retrieval stage, CLAIMNOVtakes
a claim c from the previous stage's list of claims,
embeds its text together with its paper's title with
text-embedding-3-large, and produces a set of
relevant pool claims R(c) for comparison to that
claim.
To obtain such a set, we retrieve the k-nearest
(by cosine similarity) pool claims of the same di-
mension, keeping at most one claim per pool paper.
We determine k by pool size, taking k=10 as the
minimum based on an independent retrieval valida-
tion (see Appendix O), and for larger pools we use
the heuristic k= 0.2n d, where nd is the number of
pool papers with a claim in that dimension, capped
at 40. This gives k=10 for the disguise pools and
k≈35for the anchor pools (§4.4).

During the claim entailment stage, CLAIMNOV
judges the entailment of every pair (c, c′) for c′ ∈
R(c) with an LLM (gpt-4o-mini at temperature
0), giving titles and abstracts of pool papers as
context.
The judge rates the extent to which the pool
claim entails or covers the proposal claim on an
ordinal scale ℓ(c, c′)∈ {1, . . . ,5}: 1 unrelated, 2
shared topic only, 3 partial coverage with impor-
tant details differing, 4 strong coverage with minor
details missing, and 5 full coverage of the claim's
substantive content. We map these levels onto the
unit interval by taking e(c, c′) = (ℓ(c, c′)−1)/4∈
[0,1].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Ground truth is anchored in publication timelines, reviewer-attributed prior art, and multi-annotator human audits, with cross-family labeler checks and repeated runs.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported on larger held-out datasets: 380 disguised proposals, 400 later-realized ideas, 160 claim-disputed proposals, and 100 hybrid proposals.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: System prompts, dimension weights, retrieval depth, and decision thresholds were tuned on small pilot subsets, including 20 disputed pairs, 32 decoys, and a 20-paper extraction ground truth.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that whole-proposal checks suffer high false-alarm rates or reject incremental work while CLAIMNOV preserves partially novel ideas and achieves higher informedness (J=0.95 vs CoI-Agent's 0.93) are well-supported by empirical data.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation thoroughly compares CLAIMNOV against seven existing novelty checks across proposal catch rates, false alarm rates, and claim-level attribution accuracy. Extensive ablations, cross-family judge checks, and human verification audits substantiate the quantitative findings.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation uses objective ground-truth constructions (ICML/NeurIPS publication timelines, verified ICLR review disputes, and multi-annotator human validation audits).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established on large held-out benchmark datasets (380 disguised proposals, 400 later-realized proposals, 160 reviewer disputes, and 100 hybrid spliced proposals).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: System prompts and heuristic thresholds were calibrated using pilot subsets (such as 20 disputed pairs and 32 decoys) and GEPA prompt tuning on a small extraction dataset.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate limitations, including reliance on fixed-pool retrieval rather than live web search, domain restriction to AI research, heuristics in dimension weighting, and the eventual decay of temporal cutoffs.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology decomposes research proposals into typed claims, retrieves same-dimension prior art claims, computes graded entailment, and aggregates them into a structured novelty profile evaluated by a verdict judge. The evaluation framework establishes temporal ground truth via disguised post-cutoff papers, historical ICLR reviewer disputes, and post-cutoff later-realized ideas.
primary.quality_rationale: The work addresses an important failure mode in autonomous scientific discovery pipelines with sound methodology, comprehensive benchmarking, robust statistical comparisons, and solid empirical grounding.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces an evaluation framework with temporal ground truth (1,060 proposals) for scientific novelty checking in AI pipelines, audits seven existing systems, and proposes CLAIMNOV, a claim-level novelty module.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work addresses an important failure mode in autonomous scientific discovery pipelines with sound methodology, comprehensive benchmarking, robust statistical comparisons, and solid empirical grounding.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Two distinct judge families agree on agent ranking (Kendall tau = 0.87), controlled deletions selectively lower targeted question scores while padding produces no detectable gain, and a blinded first-author audit corroborates sampled checkpoint decisions.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by two LLM judge pipelines, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GPT-6-luna, scoring frozen evidence-linked checkpoints.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evaluated agents are pre-trained LLMs run in a fixed ReAct harness; no training, tuning, or selection against RubricAtlas rubrics or judge outputs is reported.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully bounded and well aligned with empirical results; the authors distinguish analytical completeness from argument validity, show that single-reference rubrics underrepresent question types, and explicitly report where generic validity diagnostics exhibit low cross-judge agreement.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation of the benchmark includes two separate LLM judge pipelines achieving high checkpoint agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.71) and agent-ranking agreement (Kendall tau = 0.87) across ten deep research agents, sensitivity tests to reference report selection, controlled text perturbations (deletions and padding), and a blinded first-author audit.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Cross-judge agreement between two distinct model families (GPT and DeepSeek) shows strong rank correlation (Kendall tau = 0.87), controlled perturbations demonstrate selective sensitivity to deleted target content with no gain from padding, and a blinded domain-informed human author audit corroborates checkpoint assignments.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The final evaluation is established by two LLM judge pipelines (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GPT-6-luna) scoring evidence-aligned binary checkpoints derived from the frozen RubricAtlas hierarchy.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evaluated agents operate using general pre-trained backbones in a fixed ReAct harness without being trained or fine-tuned against the RubricAtlas rubrics or judge pipelines.

primary.limitations: The authors thoroughly discuss limitations, including the lack of external expert validation beyond the first-author audit, the domain/language focus on Chinese financial reports, the potential sensitivity to prompt design or model families, and the residual unmeasured effects of web browsing randomness.
primary.method_assessment: The method constructs type-level rubrics through an automated multi-step LLM pipeline aggregating questions across reports within domain families, freezing the rubrics prior to evaluation, and using two distinct LLM judge pipelines with explicit evidence alignment and negative criteria.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript provides a methodologically rigorous, highly self-critical evaluation benchmark. The experiments systematically address threats to validity, such as padding attacks, deletion responses, and reference-selection bias, and transparently document performance across multiple LLM judges and human audit samples.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RubricAtlas, an evaluation framework and dataset derived from 3,079 Chinese financial research reports across 99 research types, structuring evaluation into type-level analytical questions, targets, and evidence-linked binary checkpoints.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript provides a methodologically rigorous, highly self-critical evaluation benchmark. The experiments systematically address threats to validity, such as padding attacks, deletion responses, and reference-selection bias, and transparently document performance across multiple LLM judges and human audit samples.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors thoroughly discuss limitations, including the lack of external expert validation beyond the first-author audit, the domain/language focus on Chinese financial reports, the potential sensitivity to prompt design or model families, and the residual unmeasured effects of web browsing randomness.
